ceramic.title: What Is a LEI (Legal Entity Identifier)? Definition, Examples & How It Works
ceramic.snippet:
What Is a LEI (Legal Entity Identifier)? Definition, Examples & How It Works

 LEI (Legal Entity Identifier) 

  What Is a LEI (Legal Entity Identifier)? (Short Answer) 

 A  Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) is a  20-character alphanumeric code that uniquely identifies a legally distinct organization participating in financial markets. Each LEI links to standardized reference data-like the entity’s legal name, registered address, and ownership structure. The system is global and governed by the  Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation (GLEIF) .

 You won’t see an LEI scrolling across CNBC tickers. But behind the scenes, it’s one of the quiet pieces of plumbing that keeps modern markets from breaking. When regulators, clearinghouses, and institutional investors want to know  who exactly is on the other side of a trade, the LEI is how they know.

   In one sentence: An LEI is a globally standardized ID that tells the market exactly which legal entity is involved in a financial transaction.   Why it matters: It reduces counterparty confusion, improves risk tracking, and makes it harder for systemic risks to hide in complex corporate structures.   When you’ll encounter it: Mutual fund filings, bond prospectuses, derivatives disclosures, EMIR/MiFID reports, and institutional ownership data.   Important nuance: An LEI identifies the  entity , not the security-stocks and bonds still use ISINs, CUSIPs, or tickers.   Historical note: LEIs were created after the  2008 financial crisis to fix regulators’ inability to see interconnected risks in real time.   Surprising fact: LEIs must be  renewed annually ; an expired LEI is still visible but flagged as inactive. 

   LEI (Legal Entity Identifier) Explained 

   What Drives LEI (Legal Entity Identifier) Usage? 

 Now flip it.

  BlackRock Fund Complex (ongoing): Each ETF and mutual fund has its own LEI, even though they share a parent. This allows regulators to distinguish risk at the product level.

octen.title: Saba Asks Judge to Block BlackRock From Using Contentious Bylaw - Bloomberg
octen.snippet:
Weinstein’s Saba Argues Against BlackRock Hold on Fund Board
- Judge to decide if asset manager is skewing trustee elections
- Saba says it’s being kept off board depite owning 27% of fund
This article is for subscribers only.
Saba Capital Management asked a federal judge to block BlackRock Inc. from using a bylaw that Boaz Weinstein’s firm says is keeping it from having a voice in a closed-end fund despite acquiring a substantial stake.
At a Wednesday court hearing, Saba argued that BlackRock is using the bylaw to keep un-elected trustees at its ESG Capital Allocation Trust in place indefinitely, skirting a federal law requiring at least two-thirds of a fund board to be elected by shareholders. Saba acquired a stake in the $1.9 billion fund in 2022, but says the entire board was appointed by BlackRock.
